newsitem.title: USA: Mass. says Sept revenues firm 1.1 pct to $1.28 bln.
newsitem.headline: Mass. says Sept revenues firm 1.1 pct to $1.28 bln.

text.p: Massachusetts on Wednesday said that tax revenues rose to $1.28 billion in September, which means the state is on target to hit its goal for the 1997 fiscal year.
During this fiscal year, the state has collected $2.87 billion, about 2.6 percent more than last year, and the latest data for September marks a 1.1 percent increase above the year-ago period.
"The monthly collections for September bring total reveneus for this fiscal year within the benchmark range," said Revenue Commissioner Mitchell Adams.
In September, Massachusetts collected $674.1 million from income taxes, an increase of $47.7 million, and $443.6 million in witholding taxes, a $38.8 million rise.
From sales and use taxes, the state gathered $223.9 million, up $24.6 million. And corporate tax collections rose $30.7 million to $159.8 million.
